newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rate drops on high kuna supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rate drops on high kuna supply.

text.p: The Croatian interbank call money rate dropped to 10 percent on Monday from 11 percent amid high supply of kuna funds, dealers said.
They said state bank HBOR lent call money funds at an even lower rate of 9.0 percent.
"The balance on banks' accounts rose yesterday which led to exceptionally high supply today," Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She said 11.5 million were settled in the morning trade, leaving some 70 million surplus.
One-month interbank loans were made at 13 percent.
Overnight trade totalled a meagre 0.16 million kuna on Monday as one bank borrowed money to square its position while all others were positive. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
